children: has landed on Citi's 90-day upside catalyst watch ahead of its September 23 Connect event, with the bank expecting fresh AI and product updates to strengthen the case for further gains. Citi analyst Ronald Josey kept a Buy rating and $800 price target, implying about 19.4% upside from Meta's latest close, as accelerating product launches and early adoption of its Muse models bolster confidence in returns from heavy AI spending.

Citi's catalyst watch runs through December 15, giving investors a clear near-term window to assess whether Meta can turn its expanding AI investments into more visible product and revenue opportunities.
Josey expects Connect to bring updates on Muse, next-generation AI models and Meta's smart-glasses strategy.
Those developments matter because Meta's investment case increasingly rests on AI improving both sides of its business: consumer engagement and advertiser returns.
Citi also highlighted Meta's expanding AI use cases across personal, business and enterprise applications, suggesting the company's opportunity extends beyond its core social-media platforms.

At the same time, the bank remains constructive on Meta's existing advertising engine. Improving Reels monetization, large user scale, engagement growth and continued advertising innovation all support Citi's valuation thesis.

That combination gives Meta a stronger base than many companies spending aggressively on AI because the company can fund development through a highly profitable advertising business while testing new products across billions of users.
Connect is the next major test of whether Meta's AI spending is translating into tangible products rather than simply higher capital expenditures.
Investors should watch Muse adoption, new AI features, the roadmap for Meta glasses and any signs that those products can eventually generate meaningful revenue.
The strongest outcome would be evidence that AI is simultaneously lifting engagement, advertising monetization and new-product adoption.

The risks remain familiar: weaker digital-ad spending, regulatory pressure, tougher competition and limited financial contribution from businesses outside advertising. If Connect shows meaningful progress on monetization, Citi's $800 target could gain stronger support.

title: Citi Sees Bigger Opportunity Ahead for Meta Stock
